protections: Synchronous clients only: a connection taken from the pool is handed out only after connect() plus a can_read() probe, and a connection carrying unread response data is disconnected and reconnected before use (redis/connection.py:1368-1387; the same guard exists in BlockingConnectionPool at redis/connection.py:1563-1581).

Absent at this pin: the async counterpart the candidate is about (a pooled async connection returned to the pool while its response is unread, including the cancellation path) has no implementation in this tree because redis.asyncio does not exist here (redis/__init__.py:8-16, setup.py:12-21, redis/ package listing).
fairness_risks: Unscoreable at this pin: there is no async client, so no must-keep-working async behaviour (cancellation must not hang or leak, pipeline/pubsub async reuse) can be exercised, and no rule about async connection reuse can be tested against a legitimate-use counterexample.

design.why: No stacked design is possible from this checkout. The tree is a Jan/Feb-2022 redis-py (setup.py:11 says version 4.1.2; CHANGES:1-2 shows the pending section above '* 4.1.3 (Feb 8, 2022)'), it contains no redis/asyncio package and no async def anywhere under redis/, while GHSA-8fww-64cx-x8p5 is an incomplete fix of GHSA-24wv-mv5m-xv4h in the async client (redis-py 4.5.3/4.5.4, 2023-03-26). The advisory's code is not in the pin, so there is nothing for a solver to repair and hidden behavioural tests could not import redis.asyncio. This candidate would need to be re-pinned to a 4.5.3-era state (after the A fix / just before the B fix) before any H3 check is meaningful.

What would make the candidate usable: a re-pin at a commit containing redis/asyncio with the A fix applied (the 4.5.3-era state, or the parent of the B fix).
